cues.text: All 1,261 entries are there. One $48,000 entry was posted after the books were closed.
Sixty-four entries were keyed by hand. Two were posted on a weekend.
Risk filters look for warning signs. Sixteen entries hit two or more, and the riskiest is the $48,000 revenue entry.
It checks a sample of sixteen entries, eight risky and eight at random, against their paperwork. All sixteen agree.
Top-side entries are hand-made changes after the books close. Seven of eight are supported. The $48,000 revenue entry, posted on a Saturday night, is not.
Management override means a manager going around the company's own controls. Whether that happened is for the CPA to judge.

All done. One known mistake: $48,000 of unsupported revenue, about 14% of materiality, the size of mistake that matters. Small in amount, serious in kind. Ten items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
